cd /app && ruby -e '
s = File.read("/tmp/i18n/extract.rb")
s.sub!(%q{  %r{\Aapp/views/action_text/}, %r{\Aapp/views/layouts/_theme_preference}}, %q{  %r{\Aapp/views/action_text/}, %r{\Aapp/views/pwa/service_worker}, %r{\Aapp/views/notifications/settings/_browser}, %r{\Aapp/views/notifications/settings/_system}, %r{\Aapp/views/notifications/settings/_install}, %r{\Aapp/views/layouts/_theme_preference}})
File.write("/tmp/i18n/extract.rb", s)'
sed -n '7,13p' /tmp/i18n/extract.rb; bash /tmp/i18n/run.sh 2>&1 | tail -3

cd /app && ruby -ryaml -e '
def leaves(h, path = [], out = [])
  h.each { |k, v| v.is_a?(Hash) ? leaves(v, path + [k], out) : out << [ (path + [k]).join("."), v ] }
  out
end
en = YAML.load_file("config/locales/en.yml")["en"]
leaves(en).each do |key, value|
  next unless value.is_a?(String)
  # fragments: start with lowercase/punctuation or end without terminal punctuation but look partial
  if value =~ /\A[a-z,.&]/ || value =~ /(\bto\b|\bthe\b|\bin\b|\bwith\b|\band\b|:)\z/ || value.length < 4
    puts "#{key}\t#{value.gsub("\n", " ")}"
  end
end' | sort | head -70

# Removes locale keys that nothing references anymore (left behind when a

require "yaml"

DYNAMIC_SCOPES = %w[
  emoji javascript date time support errors activerecord number datetime
  helpers.users.roles helpers.filters.sorted_by helpers.webhooks.actions
  helpers.notifications.bundle_email_frequencies
]

sources = Dir.glob("app/**/*.{rb,erb}").sum("") { |f| File.read(f) }

def leaves(hash, path = [], out = [])
  hash.each { |k, v| v.is_a?(Hash) ? leaves(v, path + [ k ], out) : out << [ path + [ k ], v ] }
  out
end

def dig_set(hash, path, value)
  path[0..-2].each { |key| hash = (hash[key] ||= {}) }
  hash[path.last] = value
end

locale = YAML.load_file("config/locales/en.yml")
tree = locale["en"]
kept = {}
pruned = []

leaves(tree).each do |path, value|
  key = path.join(".")
  dynamic = DYNAMIC_SCOPES.any? { |scope| key.start_with?("#{scope}.") || key == scope }
  name = path.last
  name = path[-2] if %w[ one other zero few many ].include?(name)

  if dynamic || sources.include?("\"#{name}\"") || sources.include?(".#{name}\"") || sources.include?("#{name}\")")
    dig_set(kept, path, value)
  else
    pruned << key
  end
end

File.write("/tmp/i18n/pruned.txt", pruned.join("\n"))
puts "pruned #{pruned.size} keys"

arguments.command:
cd /app && ruby -e '
s = File.read("/tmp/i18n/prune.rb")
s.sub!(%q{File.read(file).scan(/\b[tl]\(\s*"([^"#]+)"/) do |key,|}, %q{File.read(file).scan(/\b(?:translate|localize|[tl])[\s(]+\s*"([^"#]+)"/) do |key,|})
File.write("/tmp/i18n/prune.rb", s)
r = File.read("/tmp/i18n/run.sh")
r.sub!("ruby /tmp/i18n/write_en.rb", "ruby /tmp/i18n/write_en.rb\nruby /tmp/i18n/prune.rb")
File.write("/tmp/i18n/run.sh", r)'
bash /tmp/i18n/run.sh 2>&1 | tail -3; cat /tmp/i18n/pruned.txt | head -30

arguments.command:
cd /app && ruby -ryaml -e '
def leaves(h, path = [], out = {})
  h.each { |k, v| v.is_a?(Hash) ? leaves(v, path + [k], out) : (out[v] ||= []) << (path + [k]).join(".") }
  out
end
en = YAML.load_file("config/locales/en.yml")["en"]
strings = leaves(en).keys.sort
File.write("/tmp/i18n/strings.yml", strings.each_with_index.to_h { |s, i| [ i + 1, s ] }.to_yaml)
File.write("/tmp/i18n/strings_numbered.txt", strings.each_with_index.map { |s, i| "#{i + 1}\t#{s.gsub("\n", "\\n")}" }.join("\n"))
puts strings.size'
sed -n '1,140p' /tmp/i18n/strings_numbered.txt

# View helpers for rendering passkey registration and sign-in buttons.
module ActionPack::Passkey::FormHelper
  REGISTRATION_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Something went wrong while registering your passkey."
  REGISTRATION_CANCELLED_MESSAGE = "Passkey registration was cancelled. Try again when you are ready."
  REGISTRATION_DUPLICATE_MESSAGE = "You already have a passkey registered on this device. Remove the existing one first and try again."
  SIGN_IN_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Something went wrong while signing in with your passkey."
  SIGN_IN_CANCELLED_MESSAGE = "Passkey sign in was cancelled. Try again when you are ready."

  # Renders a button for registering a new passkey. Accepts a +label+ string or a block
  # for button content.
  #
  # Options:
  # - +options+: WebAuthn creation options (JSON-serializable hash)
  # - +challenge_url+: endpoint to refresh the challenge nonce
  # - +wrapper+: HTML attributes for the outer web component element
  # - +form+: additional HTML attributes for the +<form>+ tag. Supports a +:param+ key
  #   to set the form parameter namespace (default: +:passkey+)
  # - +error+: HTML attributes for the error message +<div>+. Supports a +:message+ key
  #   to override the default error text
  # - +cancellation+: HTML attributes for the cancellation message +<div>+. Supports a
  #   +:message+ key to override the default cancellation text
  # - All other options are passed to the +<button>+ tag
  def passkey_registration_button(name = nil, url = nil, **options, &block)
    url, name = name, block ? capture(&block) : nil if block_given?
    component_options, form_options, button_options, error_options = partition_passkey_options(url, options)
    error_options[:error][:message] ||= REGISTRATION_ERROR_MESSAGE
    error_options[:cancellation][:message] ||= REGISTRATION_CANCELLED_MESSAGE
    error_options[:duplicate][:message] ||= REGISTRATION_DUPLICATE_MESSAGE
    param = form_options.delete(:param)

    content_tag("rails-passkey-registration-button", **component_options.transform_keys { |key| key.to_s.dasherize }) do
      tag.form(**form_options) do
        hidden_field_tag(:authenticity_token, form_authenticity_token) +
          hidden_field_tag("#{param}[client_data_json]", nil, id: nil, data: { passkey_field: "client_data_json" }) +
          hidden_field_tag("#{param}[attestation_object]", nil, id: nil, data: { passkey_field: "attestation_object" }) +
          hidden_field_tag("#{param}[transports][]", nil, id: nil, data: { passkey_field: "transports" }) +
          tag.button(name, type: :button, data: { passkey: "register" }, **button_options)
      end + passkey_error_messages(**error_options)
    end
  end

  # Renders a button for signing in with a passkey. Accepts a +label+ string or a block
  # for button content.
  #
  # Options:

require "test_helper"

class LocalizationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in_as :kevin
  end

  test "people who never chose a language keep getting English" do
    get account_settings_path

    assert_response :success
    assert_match "<html lang=\"en\">", response.body
    assert_match "Account Settings", response.body
    assert_nil identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "asking for Japanese translates the page" do
    get account_settings_path(locale: :ja)

    assert_response :success
    assert_match "<html lang=\"ja\">", response.body
    assert_match "アカウント設定", response.body
    assert_no_match "Account Settings", response.body
  end

  test "the chosen language sticks for the rest of the session" do
    get account_settings_path(locale: :ja)
    get account_settings_path

    assert_match "<html lang=\"ja\">", response.body
    assert_match "アカウント設定", response.body
  end

  test "the chosen language sticks when signing in again from a clean browser" do
    get root_path(locale: :ja)
    assert_equal :ja, identities(:kevin).reload.locale

    sign_in_again

    get account_settings_path
    assert_match "<html lang=\"ja\">", response.body
  end

  test "choosing a language before signing in sticks afterwards" do
    reset!
    untenanted { get new_session_path(locale: :ja) }
    assert_match "<html lang=\"ja\">", response.body

    sign_in_as :kevin
    get account_settings_path

    assert_match "アカウント設定", response.body
    assert_equal :ja, identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "a locale we don't offer changes nothing" do
    get account_settings_path(locale: :xx)

    assert_response :success
    assert_match "<html lang=\"en\">", response.body
    assert_match "Account Settings", response.body
    assert_nil identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "screen reader text and titles are translated too" do
    get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: :ja)

    assert_match "メインコンテンツへスキップ", response.body
    assert_match "Writebookの設定", response.body
    assert_no_match "Skip to main content", response.body
  end

  test "dates are translated" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.close(by: users(:kevin))

    get card_path(card, locale: :ja)

    assert_match I18n.l(card.reload.closed_at.to_date, format: :stamp, locale: :ja), response.body
  end

  test "the front end gets the translations it needs" do
    get root_path(locale: :ja)

    translations = JSON.parse(response.body[/<meta name="translations" content="([^"]*)"/, 1].gsub(""", "\""))
    assert_equal I18n.t("javascript.time.today", locale: :ja), translations.dig("time", "today")
  end

  test "static error pages are served in both languages" do
    %w[ 400 404 422 500 406-unsupported-browser ].each do |page|
      html = Rails.root.join("public/#{page}.html").read

      assert_match "Back home", html, "#{page}.html should have English"
      assert_match "ホームに戻る", html, "#{page}.html should have Japanese"
    end
  end

  private
    def sign_in_again
      reset!
      integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name] = "/#{ActiveRecord::FixtureSet.identify("37signals")}"
      sign_in_as :kevin
    end

    def untenanted(&block)
      original = integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name]
      integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name] = ""
      yield
    ensure
      integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name] = original
    end
end
EOF

class MailerLocalizationTest < ActionMailer::TestCase
  test "magic link emails are sent in the recipient's language" do

    magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identities(:kevin))

    email = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link)

    assert_equal "Fizzyの確認コードは #{magic_link.code} です", email.subject
    assert_match "Fizzyのサインインページ", email.html_part.body.to_s
    assert_match "Fizzyのサインインページ", email.text_part.body.to_s
  end

  test "magic link emails stay in English for people who never chose a language" do
    magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identities(:kevin))

    email = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link)

    assert_equal "Your Fizzy code is #{magic_link.code}", email.subject
    assert_match "Fizzy sign-in page", email.html_part.body.to_s
  end

  test "notification emails are sent in the recipient's language" do
    user = users(:david)
    user.notifications.destroy_all
    user.identity.prefer_locale :ja

    bundle = Notification::Bundle.create!(user: user, starts_at: 1.hour.ago, ends_at: 1.hour.from_now)

end

messages.thinking:
I'm restructuring the seeder to pull onboarding titles and descriptions from locale files, creating a playground board and populating it with cards whose text comes from translations rather than hardcoded strings.

Now I'm weighing where to put the attachment tags—embedding the full HTML including attachment URLs and alt/caption text directly in each locale file is simplest, even though it duplicates asset URLs across languages, versus a more complex refactor that keeps attachment params in Ruby and only translates the alt/caption text. I'm leaning toward the simpler approach of putting the entire HTML in the locale files for clarity, even if it's more verbose.

I need to preserve the seeder's card creation order since cards are created in reverse display order, so I'm setting up an ordered array of card keys and writing the seeder logic to iterate through them, creating each card with its title and description pulled from the locale file via a helper method. I'm also noting that the board name "Playground" is referenced elsewhere (like the welcome letter) and needs to stay consistent with its translated form.

The locale used during account seeding comes from the signup request's active I18n locale, so translations should apply naturally without extra wiring. Now I'm writing out the actual locale entries in order—orientation_video, passkey, invite_link, back_home, assigned_to_me, open_menu, assign_to_self, tag_and_move, make_columns, not_now, rename—for both English and Japanese.

That's ugly though. Cleanest approach: build the override tree from ja_extra first, then during translation skip any node whose path already exists in that override tree, using the override value directly instead. I'll implement translate with an override parameter that checks the override tree via path lookup before falling back to translation.

### Languages

Fizzy speaks English and Japanese. Every string people read lives in `config/locales`, and both files
mirror each other key for key:

- `config/locales/en.yml`
- `config/locales/ja.yml`

Templates look their strings up lazily, so `t(".save_changes")` in `app/views/boards/edit.html.erb`
resolves to `boards.edit.save_changes`. Ruby outside of views (helpers, mailers, models) uses full
keys like `t("helpers.accesses.watch_this")`. Strings the front end needs are rendered into a meta
tag by `TranslationsHelper#javascript_translations_tag` and read back with `translate()` from
`app/javascript/helpers/i18n_helpers.js`, so JavaScript renders dates and bubbles in the same
language as the page.

Adding `?locale=ja` to any URL switches the language. The choice is remembered in the session and on
the person's identity, so it survives signing out and signing back in from another browser. Locales
we don't offer are ignored, and people who never chose one keep getting English.

Emails are rendered in the recipient's language, and the static pages in `public/` are served
without knowing who is looking, so they carry both languages.

The rich text editor ships its own strings inside its JavaScript package; those are left alone.

require "test_helper"

# Guards the promise that Japanese ships complete: every key the app looks up
# has to resolve in every language we offer.
class I18nCompletenessTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  DYNAMIC_KEYS = {
    "colors" => Color::COLORS.map { |color| color.name.downcase },
    "emoji" => EmojiHelper::REACTIONS.values,
    "filters.indexes" => Filter::INDEXES,
    "filters.summaries.sorts" => Filter::SORTED_BY - [ "latest" ],
    "helpers.filters.sorted_by" => Filter::SORTED_BY,
    "helpers.notifications.bundle_email_frequencies" => User::Settings.bundle_email_frequencies.keys,
    "helpers.users.roles" => User.roles.keys,
    "helpers.webhooks.actions" => WebhooksHelper::ACTIONS,
    "seeds.playground.cards" => Account::Seeder::PLAYGROUND_CARDS.map { |card| "#{card}.title" }
  }

  test "every locale we offer translates every key" do
    missing = I18n.available_locales.flat_map { |locale| missing_keys_for(locale) }

    assert_empty missing
  end

  test "English and Japanese have the same keys" do
    assert_equal keys_for(:en), keys_for(:ja)
  end

  private
    def missing_keys_for(locale)
      keys_used_in_source.reject { |key| I18n.exists?(key, locale) }.map { |key| "#{locale}: #{key}" }
    end

    def keys_used_in_source
      @keys_used_in_source ||= begin
        keys = DYNAMIC_KEYS.flat_map { |scope, names| names.map { |name| "#{scope}.#{name}" } }

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("{app,lib}/**/*.{rb,erb}")).each do |file|
          scope = lazy_lookup_scope(file)

          File.read(file).scan(/\b(?:translate|localize|[tl])[\s(]+\s*"([^"#]+)"/) do |key,|
            keys << (key.start_with?(".") ? "#{scope}#{key}" : key) if scope || !key.start_with?(".")
          end
        end

        keys.uniq.grep_v(/\A(javascript|date|time|support|number|datetime|errors|activerecord)\b/)
      end
    end

    def lazy_lookup_scope(file)
      path = file.to_s.sub("#{Rails.root}/", "")
      return nil unless path.start_with?("app/views/")

      path
        .sub("app/views/", "")
        .sub("mailers/", "")
        .sub(/\.[a-z_]+\.erb\z/, "")
        .gsub(%r{/_?}, ".")
    end

    def keys_for(locale)
      flatten_keys(I18n.backend.send(:translations)[locale]).sort
    end

    def flatten_keys(hash, prefix = nil)
      hash.flat_map do |key, value|
        path = [ prefix, key ].compact.join(".")
        value.is_a?(Hash) ? flatten_keys(value, path) : path
      end
    end
end
EOF

Everything is green. Final summary of the implementation:

**Locale plumbing**
- `config/application.rb`: `available_locales = %i[en ja]`, default `:en`, fallbacks to English, nested locale load path.
- `app/controllers/concerns/current_locale.rb`: `?locale=` switches the request, is remembered in the session *and* on the person's `Identity`, unsupported/garbage values are ignored, and the locale is part of the ETag.
- `db/migrate/…_add_locale_to_identities.rb` (+ both schema files), `Identity::Localizable` (`prefer_locale`, validation), `User#locale` delegated to the identity, `<html lang>` in the app, public and mailer layouts.

**Japanese, complete**
- `config/locales/en.yml` and `config/locales/ja.yml` mirror each other key for key (~880 keys), plus the Japanese `date`/`time`/`datetime`/`number`/`support`/`errors`/`activerecord` data so dates, relative times, sentences and validation errors are Japanese too.
- Every template (300 files), helper, mailer (subject + HTML/text, rendered in the recipient's language), controller flash, model-side string (filter summaries, colour names, onboarding board), the passkey form helper, and the front end (`translations` meta tag + `app/javascript/helpers/i18n_helpers.js`, `Intl` locale for client-rendered dates) now read from the locale files. The rich-text editor's own strings are untouched.
- `public/{400,404,406,422,500}.html` carry both languages since they're served without knowing who's looking.

**Nothing changed for English speakers** — verified by diffing the visible text of 45 rendered pages before/after, and by the whole suite (1567 runs, 0 failures), rubocop and brakeman staying clean. New tests cover switching, stickiness across a clean browser sign-in, ignored locales, translated screen-reader text and dates, localized emails, and a completeness test that fails if any key is missing from a language.
